Abstract
While practicing qigong in natural settings reportedly enhances its benefits, the influence of specific landscape attributes has not been studied extensively. According to the Landscape Preference Matrix, coherence and complexity are key factors in determining environmental preference. Unlike research on meditation, which considers complexity (such as plant diversity), studies on qigong tend to focus more on coherence, leaving the role of complexity and its potential impact on practice efficacy in urban settings un

be traded off against each other.

Abstract
Climate change is one of the major drivers of changes in the natural habitats of many insect pests worldwide. The white-striped longhorn beetle Batocera lineolata Chevrolat, 1852 (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae) is a serious pest species currently causing severe damage to Eucalyptus L’Hér., 1789 (Myrtales: Myrtaceae) plantation forests in Northern Vietnam. Understanding the geographical distribution characteristics of this pest is important for forest management

ncerning B. lineolata in Vietnam.

Abstract
Residential outdoor landscapes constitute the most frequently encountered visual environment for urban residents, yet systematic evaluation of their aesthetic quality and ecological service value remains lacking. This study developed an integrated three-stage framework combining deep learning semantic segmentation, the Scenic Beauty Estimation method, and machine learning regression modeling to assess public visual aesthetic preference for residential outdoor landscapes, understood as one measurable component of the cultural ecosystem services provided by urban residential green spaces. However, a highly structured GI does not necessarily correspond to high bird habitat (BH) suitability, and existing research has paid relatively little attention to the spatial congruence and mismatch relationships between the two, and how these can be further translated into ecological network planning strategies.
